answer: A social-graph defense treats each agent as a vertex in an attestation web and weights its influence by how few vouching hops separate it from trusted anchors. A sybil can mint endless fake vertices, but each still needs an edge from a real staked voucher who risks slashing for lying. So the attacker's fakes pile up far out like a shifting dune with no path to the summit of trust, and buying genuine edges costs real stake per identity, making mass forgery priced out instead of free.
